Notes from proxy logs (09:30–09:40):
- Observed a spike in CONNECT timeouts from our edge to one peering cluster (peer-az2). Timeout count aligns with Crestline's error window.
- DNS resolution attempts for crestline.service.internal show repeated NXDOMAIN then successful after ~600–1200ms for affected flows.
- Proxy CPU and connection queue depth spiked briefly on host proxy-az2-14; we saw a surge of SYNs from the peer side.

Hypothesis: Transient routing amplification at the peering fabric caused DNS resolver backpressure and proxy queue growth => cascading 5xxs.

I am pushing full tcpdumps and filtered log extracts to the Drive link. Moving to correlate with BGP/peering events.

—Marissa

Date: 2026-11-29T10:18:00-08:00
Subject: RE: Sudden increase in 5xxs + token latency — urgent

Quick routing update:
- Peering telemetry shows a short-lived flapping on the VXLAN overlay to Crestline's peer (peer-az2). One of their route-reflectors toggled a path that caused ~40s of asymmetric paths to a subset of edge nodes.
- Asymmetric flows hit a firewall/proxy cluster where stateful sessions were rehydrated -> several TCP resets and downstream application timeouts.

Mitigation applied at 10:05 PST: we blackholed the transient peer path and pushed traffic to fallback peering (peer-az1). Error rate dropped to ~0.9% by 10:12 and p95 latency returned toward baseline by 10:22.

Next steps: need a post-mortem and exec note. Sylvia requested an exec-level summary and timeline.

—Jonas

Team — execs at Crestline are demanding a succinct timeline and an indication of whether we require policy/network changes on their side. Draft below for visibility; please edit and approve so I can send to Crestline and our VP.

Draft exec summary (please keep to 3–4 bullets):
- 08:55 PST: Crestline reported a sudden rise in inference 5xxs and token latency affecting production traffic (error rate ~7%).
- 09:30–09:40 PST: Our proxy logs and DNS traces indicated elevated DNS latency and proxy queue exhaustion tied to a peering cluster (peer-az2).
- 10:05 PST: We rerouted traffic off the transient peering path to fallback peering (peer-az1); errors fell to ~0.9% by 10:12 and latency normalized by 10:22.
- Root cause hypothesis: transient peering instability produced asymmetric routing into a stateful proxy/firewall cluster, producing DNS/backpressure cascades. Post-mortem pending.

Attachments: draft_exec_note.docx (contains timeline, traces, and suggested follow-ups).

Please reply with edits ASAP — Crestline execs want this in the next hour.

Date: 2026-11-29T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-incident: Crestline — confirmed routing flap + follow-ups

Final update for thread (post incident review complete):
- Root cause: intermittent BGP/route-reflector instability at Crestline's peering fabric produced duplicate/asymmetric advertisement that overwhelmed one of our proxy clusters.
- Impact window: 08:55–10:22 PST. Peak error rate ~7%.
- Action taken: immediate reroute to fallback peering, increased DNS resolver parallelism, and tightened proxy connection queue thresholds to avoid head-of-line blocking.
- Required from Crestline: their network team to confirm and patch RR config to prevent rapid route churn; recommend route dampening for the affected hash-space.
- Internal follow-ups: automated peering failover will get an additional health-check gate; SRE will add a synthetic check that alerts on DNS lookup latency >300ms for high-traffic customers.

Sylvia — attaching the exec note and timeline. Happy to run a joint post-mortem with your network team tomorrow 09:00 PST.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
SRE, Redwood Inference
